content.title: About
content.content: Red radish is a small, crunchy root vegetable with a bright red skin that is typically eaten raw. It has a mildly peppery, refreshing flavor and a juicy texture. Radishes are grown in temperate climates and are commonly used in salads, snacks, and as a garnish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Radishes belong to the Brassicaceae family, making them relatives of cabbage, broccoli, and mustard.
The red color comes from anthocyanins, natural antioxidants.
Both the root and the greens of radish are edible and nutritious.
Ancient cultures used radish as a medicinal plant to aid digestion.
There are over 200 varieties of radish differing in shape, flavor, and color.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Radishes provide a high amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Low‑calorie source of fiber
items.content: Their low calorie content and dietary fiber help promote satiety and healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium aids in fluid balance and supports normal heart function.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Anthocyanins and other phytochemicals in red radish help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Radishes contain modest amounts of calcium and magnesium, important for bone strength.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to radish, resulting in itching or swelling.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Consuming large amounts may cause bloating in people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Contact dermatitis
items.content: Radish juice can irritate the skin, especially with prolonged contact.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Radishes are usually eaten raw, sliced thinly into rounds or wedges for salads, with dips, or on sandwiches. They can also be pickled or used as a colorful garnish for dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store radishes in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or a container with a small amount of moisture. Properly stored, they stay fresh for up to 2 weeks. Discard any that become soft, develop spots, or emit an off odor.
